One form is the opposite problem and is not the mis-selection pattern: Brianda Sandoval's job 37206 (XTO, Shackelford Spraberry Unit 4103H, 11/21 03:17 PM) has the "What did we observe?" multi-select entirely empty — no observation items selected at all, including no stop-work item. Her own narrative on that form describes a normal first break with no gas detected, so nothing suggests an event went unrecorded; the field was simply left unselected. It is listed again under documentation issues below.

clean.text: 1099 Kedrick McCarter filed an H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form for Ovintiv UL Cathedral 36 with all thirty photos captured on 11/21, FR answered Yes and nothing requiring attention. Brianda Sandoval's two Trailer Inspection Forms for trailer 602 were complete, same-day and fully photographed, and her 06:07 AM comment is exactly the kind of note that makes a discrepancy traceable. 1099 Robert Henigan's Trailer Readiness Form for 602 carried complete pressure and hydro entries on all four charged bottles and correctly raised the gauge lens. 1099 Rolando Flores documented seven consecutive night shifts at Buzz Hurt 36 with zero gas throughout and a written summary for every shift. Brey Rasco, Tyrell Sanders and 1099 Robbie Henigan each filed their required job or daily paperwork on time; their individual items are listed above.

Trailer forms of both kinds and the equipment sections of the H2S daily are photo-based, so a defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, not as text, and cannot be checked here. Separately, 1099 Marcos Morales's H2S daily could not be opened at all because the attachment exceeds the mail connector's size limit, so every field on that form — FR answer included — is unverified and would need to be opened directly in Outlook.

17 of 18 submissions read. The job board was available: the 11/21/2026 Ark-La-Tex and Permian Basin boards sent by Blake Walton at 10:17 AM were used, and 23 manned rows were checked for coverage — 12 on the Permian board and 11 on the Ark-La-Tex board, both from sheets still marked DRAFT. This run started at 11:06 PM Central, before the calendar day closed, so any form submitted in the final hour of 11/21 is not in these counts; the usual follow-up search of the next morning's mail could not be run because 11/22 had not yet begun, and missing Trailer Readiness Forms are the finding most often resolved by a late submission.
